title: GraphQL-Driven Selective Binary Deserialization with Custom Amazon Ion Reader
subtitle: Forking amazon-ion/ion-java to implement IonReaderBinaryUserXSelective: skipping unqueried binary payload fields directly at the wire parser level for sub-millisecond GraphQL queries.
overview: When clients execute sparse GraphQL or REST scalar projections requesting only a few fields (e.g., patient name and status from a 150-field clinical record), traditional application layers deserialize the full binary blob into heap memory before filtering out unwanted fields. To eliminate this memory allocation and CPU overhead, we contributed a selective binary streaming reader to our internal fork of Amazon Ion (`arogya-life/ion-java`). By pairing `IonReaderBinaryUserXSelective` with an endpoint GraphQL field selector tree, our data layer skips unselected struct and list bytes directly in binary wire format without ever hydrating them into Java objects.
problem: Healthcare and financial domain entities contain large nested document graphs (identifiers, extensions, codeable concepts, audit logs). In high-throughput read paths like search and autocomplete grids, clients query scalar projections requiring only 2-3 fields. Standard deserializers (Jackson, default Amazon Ion) must traverse and parse every byte, allocate nested Java objects on the JVM heap, and subject the system to heavy GC cycles. Database projections can push selections to storage, but when reading binary-encoded documents from cache grids like Infinispan or RocksDB, full document hydration creates a massive performance bottleneck.

implementation.title: 1. Upstream Fork: The IonField Hierarchical Selection Model
implementation.description: Introduced `IonField` in software.amazon.ion.impl.lite as a lightweight recursive tree modeling the client's requested selection set (matching GraphQL AST selections).

implementation.title: 2. Core Binary Parser Engine: IonReaderBinaryUserXSelective
implementation.description: Extended Amazon Ion's binary reader (`IonReaderBinaryUserX`). During `.next()`, if a struct or list field is not present in the active selection tree node, it executes an immediate `super.stepIn()` followed by `super.stepOut()`, jumping the binary pointer over child length bytes without allocating symbols or decoding values.

implementation.title: 3. Endpoint Integration: BaseResourceApi & Aspect Wire-Up
implementation.description: Exposed the scalar projection endpoint in BaseResourceApi:93. An AOP advice automatically links bidirectional parent-child references across the deserialized IonField graph before query execution.

implementation.title: 4. Zero-Hydration Streaming: ScalarSelectionQueryResultLoader
implementation.description: Connected the Infinispan cache byte layer directly to the selective reader, writing matched tokens straight into a JSON text writer without allocating intermediary domain entity POJOs.

impact: Cut API response serialization latency by over 75% for scalar and grid queries requesting subsets of domain documents.
Completely bypassed JVM heap object instantiation for unrequested fields, mitigating GC pause frequency on high-concurrency search clusters.
Achieved seamless protocol compatibility: GraphQL clients send arbitrary field masks while backend storage remains compact, raw Amazon Ion binary.
lessons: In binary formats with explicit length-prefix encoding (like Amazon Ion, Protobuf, and BSON), skipping unneeded subtrees by incrementing parser byte offsets is orders of magnitude cheaper than instantiating reflection-based POJOs.
Bitwise hierarchy tracking (`hierarchy << 1` and `hierarchy >> 1`) provides an ultra-fast O(1) mechanism for tracking nested struct depth without array or stack allocations.
